title: Relocate existing .ptsip Go tests to developer/tests

work_units.name: Inventory, migrate and rewire existing .ptsip Go tests
exact_steps: At current HEAD use tracked Git inventory to enumerate every .ptsip/**/*_test.go, including nested Go modules; record original test package, owning feature, Go module, Test/Benchmark/Fuzz/Example identifiers, fixtures, helpers, build tags, existing invocations and current verification status. Do not infer the count or owner from filenames.

Assign each file and test case to the corresponding feature responsibility under developer/tests/; create an exact source-to-target migration ledger with collision detection. Coordinate policy/contract/check, update, entry and authoring tests with the Go Authoring plan, without duplicate implementation or tests.

Inspect developer/tests/go.mod and existing test helpers and nested module boundaries. Resolve imports/replace directives and transitive dependencies without importing an inaccessible Go internal package; use exported behavior or CLI integration tests, refactor narrowly scoped testable boundaries only when necessary, and do not expose private internals merely to copy white-box tests.

Preserve all test assertions, negative cases, fixture content, setup and cleanup, build tags, package-level helper behavior and platform-specific paths; adjust fixture root discovery and temporary checkout paths. Do not copy production logic to tests to bypass integration.

Identify and update actual Go test consumers: .github/test_modes.yaml where applicable, tooling-test.yml only where necessary, policy-contract-guard.yml, policy review/applicability local runners, release verification workflows, and developer module indexes; preserve required test selection, parallelism and retired-source exclusions. Do not revive retired tests by directory-wide blanket selection or remove live checks.

Move files to the selected developer/tests responsibility subtrees; remove original _test.go only with equivalent replacement and verified execution; avoid stale duplicate test registrations and retain independent product tests under src/tests unchanged.

Run targeted Go tests at new ownership paths, then the relevant independent CI jobs and a tracked-file absence guard for .ptsip/**/*_test.go. Compare before/after named tests, assertion coverage and execution routing; report missing or skipped required tests as failures.
Record machine-readable migration ledger, commands, test evidence, remaining blockers and exact HEAD; keep transient logs out of Git and remove after review.
acceptance: Every tracked Go test under .ptsip is accounted for by an equivalent test at developer/tests; no tracked .ptsip/**/*_test.go remains.
No new tests for .ptsip functionality are authored outside developer/tests.
Go internal access and module dependencies compile on the supported Windows and CI environments; no arbitrary public exposure.
All currently required test behavior, fixtures, negative cases and actual workflow invocations are preserved and verified.
Existing retired test scope remains retired; product tests and unrelated policies remain unchanged.
Machine-readable test-location guard rejects new _test.go under .ptsip/engine/developer and detects any regression to old test roots.

verification.baseline_inventory: git ls-files with path and suffix matching under .ptsip/
